We build on top of two earlier surveys that looked at hallucinations generally within NLG.
Human evaluations are commonly viewed as the more reliable way to evaluate natural language generation (NLG) systems (in contrast to, e.g., using automatic metrics).

LLM-as-a-judge evaluations have emerged as an alternative to human evaluation due to their lower cost. This approach, made popular in machine translation evaluation, has grown in the hallucination literature from just one paper in 2023 to 40 papers (5% of hallucination papers) in 2024.

Based on a search over papers published in major NLP venues from 2019-2024, we identify 64 human evaluations of hallucination and extract key information on how evaluations are conducted (Section 3).
